text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria will restore its marine forces by 1999 in line with planned reforms in the army, Armed Forces Chief of Staff Miho Mihov said.
-- Bulgaria's Kremikovtsi steel works shareholders decided to raise capital to 200 billion levs from 18.5 billion levs and introduce a two tier management system.
-- Bulgaria's police said it arrested 14 Bulgarians in a crackdown on a drug dealing network in Sofia.
-- Bulgaria's 1997 annual inflation is seen at 700 percent, National Statistics Institute projections showed.
--Bulgaria's State Fund for Reconstruction and Development said it had placed 203 billion levs guarantees with banks which have extended credits to fund purchasing of wheat from this year's crop. @
-- Bulgaria hopes to be granted a B1 credit rating at the beginning of next year and if the country adheres strictly to reforms it may acquire BB credit rating by 1999, a Merrill Lynch report said.

-- Bulgaria's Securities and Stock Exchange Commission said it had listed the Sofia branches of ING Bank and the National Bank of Greece as investment intermediaries. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
